links.outcome: Specificity and hallucinated lesions in vLLM brain metastasis MRI reports
links.effect: Sensitivity 100% for both; specificity GPT-4o 8%, Sonnet 3.5 4%; accuracy 54% and 52%; both models hallucinated additional lesions in 12% of cases.
links.quote: Both models hallucinated additional lesions in 12% of cases.

links.outcome: Real-world clinical MRI performance of general-purpose vLLMs for brain metastasis detection
links.effect: Very low specificity (8% and 4%) and low accuracy (54% and 52%) on routine clinical MRI; authors state this precludes clinical application.
links.quote: GPT-4o and Claude Sonnet 3.5 can generate radiological reports and detect brain metastases with excellent sensitivity, but their very low specificity, frequent hallucinations, and limited spatial reliability currently preclude clinical application.

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation/benchmark of multimodal LLMs (GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet) on brain MRI metastasis detection and report generation; evaluates diagnostic performance and hallucinations without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
